source: Chen, Gilbert, Grochowski, et al. (2018), 'A genome-wide association study identifies a susceptibility locus for biliary atresia on 2p16.1 within the gene EFEMP1', PLOS Genetics 14(8):e1007532. CC0 license.
note_to_agent: This is the discovery-cohort portion of a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of biliary atresia (BA), a rare pediatric liver disease. No replication cohort or follow-up study is included here.

study_design.test: Adjusted logistic regression, additive genetic model, principal components as covariates

significance_thresholds.suggestive_significance: P < 1e-5, defined as an average of one false-positive association per GWAS

evidence_items.description: Top-associated SNP rs10865291, located in intron 5 of the EFEMP1 gene on chromosome 2p16.1.
Five additional markers in linkage disequilibrium with rs10865291 (r-squared > 0.5) also reach the suggestive significance threshold, indicating the signal is unlikely to be a genotyping artifact.
After genotype imputation, seven further SNPs in the same 2p16.1 region reach suggestive significance. rs10865291 remains the single most significant marker in the region.
A genome-wide gene-based association test (VEGAS2) was run as a complementary approach to the single-SNP tests. EFEMP1 is the top-ranked gene genome-wide, with an empirical p-value of 3.9e-5.

Across the whole genome, 19 markers total reach the suggestive significance threshold, located in 10 distinct genomic regions: 1p31.1, 1q32.2, 2p23.2, 2p16.1, 2q37.3, 3p24.2, 6p22.3, 6q24.3, 16p13.1, and 20q13.2. The 2p16.1/EFEMP1 region is one of these ten regions, not uniquely flagged at this stage relative to the other nine.
No marker anywhere in the genome, including at 2p16.1, reaches the standard genome-wide significance threshold (P < 5e-8) in this cohort.
